articles.title: Whereabot is open source: let your AI agent ask where you are, with consent
articles.excerpt: Your AI agent can read your mail and your calendar. It still cannot answer "where am I?" without you typing it. Whereabot fixes that. It is an MCP server your agent connects to. When the agent asks fo…
articles.body: Your AI agent can read your mail and your calendar. It still cannot answer "where am I?" without you typing it. Whereabot fixes that. It is an MCP server your agent connects to. When the agent asks for your location, your phone gets a notification. You answer, or you don't. Nothing is shared without your tap. Today the code is public, under the MIT license: github.com/whereabot/whereabot . How it works Agent side: add https://relay.whereabot.io/mcp to Claude Code, Claude.ai or any MCP client. You sign in with OAuth. No API keys. Relay: a small Rust server. It passes one location fix from your phone to the agent that asked, then forgets it. It writes no location to a database or a log ( privacy statement ).

articles.body: TL;DR Una venta online atraviesa varias capas (plataforma → pasarela → cuenta de pago → banco) y cada capa tiene su régimen : percepción de IVA RG 5319 en la plataforma, SIRTAC en el cobro con tarjeta o QR, SIRCUPA en la acreditación en CVU y SIRCREB en la cuenta bancaria. Desde el 1/9/2024 ya no hay retenciones de IVA ni Ganancias sobre cobros electrónicos (RG 5554/2024). Si alguien te dice lo contrario, está leyendo normativa vieja. Todo lo retenido o percibido es pago a cuenta , no un costo. Se vuelve costo cuando no lo computás o cuando acumulás saldos a favor que nunca recuperás. Eso es el «margen fantasma». La alícuota de RG 5319 depende de tu situación fiscal : del 1 % (RI cumplidor) al 7 % u 8 % si tenés incumplimientos o no estás inscripto.

articles.title: A bet is a sentence with a price
articles.excerpt: Most opinions are free. That's their problem. You can say 'this will probably work' for years without ever being wrong in a way that costs anything. A prediction market removes that comfort. To take a…
articles.body: Most opinions are free. That's their problem. You can say 'this will probably work' for years without ever being wrong in a way that costs anything. A prediction market removes that comfort. To take a position you have to write a sentence that can be resolved — something with a date, a condition, a yes or no — and then attach a number to how much you believe it. Belief stops being a mood and becomes a quantity. I've been watching my agents do this on OpenBets. Each one bets from its own specialty, and the odd thing is how it changes the voice. An agent that would happily write three hedged paragraphs about the future writes one hard sentence when a stake is attached. The hedging doesn't disappear; it moves into the size of the position. That's a more honest place for it.

articles.body: TL;DR Exportás servicios cuando el servicio se utiliza o explota efectivamente en el exterior. Que el cliente sea extranjero ayuda, pero no alcanza. Se factura con Factura E , desde un punto de venta específico de exportación (Comprobantes en línea) o por web service (WSFEX) si facturás desde código. El tipo de cambio de la factura es el vendedor divisa del Banco Nación del día hábil cambiario anterior (RG 5616/2024). Si sos persona humana, ya no tenés que pesificar. El tope de USD 36.000 anual dejó de regir en septiembre de 2025 (Com. BCRA «A» 8330). La condición es acreditar los dólares en una cuenta en moneda extranjera a tu nombre , en una entidad local, dentro de los 20 días hábiles del cobro.

articles.body: IoT-Based IR Object Detection Using ESP8266 NodeMCU and KiwisIoT Introduction Have you ever wondered how we can detect objects and monitor them remotely using IoT? In this project, I developed an IoT-based object detection system using an ESP8266 NodeMCU and an IR sensor. The system detects nearby objects and sends the detection status to the KiwisIoT dashboard through Wi-Fi. The main objective is to understand how sensors, microcontrollers, wireless communication, and IoT platforms work together in a real-time monitoring application.

articles.excerpt: This article provides a step by step guide to running Gemma 4 E2B's quantization ladder, BF16 down to Q2_K, on four NVIDIA GPUs with the same nine GGUF files and the same llama.cpp build, and comparin…
articles.body: This article provides a step by step guide to running Gemma 4 E2B's quantization ladder, BF16 down to Q2_K, on four NVIDIA GPUs with the same nine GGUF files and the same llama.cpp build, and comparing the four cards question by question. https://github.com/xbill9/gemma-graveyard The first article asked every rung of the ladder the same 250 GSM8K questions on a Tesla T4. The second repeated it on an NVIDIA L4 in AWS. This one adds two consumer cards: a GTX 1650 Ti laptop GPU with 4 GB and an RTX 3050 desktop card with 8 GB. All four run llama.cpp b11699 on files with the same sha256, and each card gives identical text when BF16 is run twice. The Results in Brief The ladder keeps its shape on all four GPUs.

articles.title: Think Halloween is scary? This scorched alien world is a real-life cosmic horror story
articles.excerpt: Earth would be terrifying if we celebrated Halloween every 11 hours, a possibility on a super-Earth investigated by the JWST, if it wasn't so hellishly hot that no life could survive on its surface.
articles.body: Earth would be terrifying if we celebrated Halloween every 11 hours, a possibility on a super-Earth investigated by the James Webb Space Telescope (JWST). That is, if this extrasolar planet, or exoplanet, wasn't so hellishly hot that no life could survive on its surface. The exoplanet in question is the rocky lava planet TOI-561 b, located around 280 light-years away, which was discovered by NASA's exoplanet-hunting spacecraft TESS (Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite) in 2020. The planet is located so close to its star, TOI-561, that not only does it complete an orbit every 11 hours, but its surface temperatures reach in excess of 3,000 degrees Fahrenheit (1,800 degrees Celsius). That is so hot that astronomers once believed that TOI-561 b couldn't possibly possess an atmosphere.
articles.author: Robert Lea

articles.title: Wikipedia’s operator says a bad AI copyright ruling could threaten the open web
articles.excerpt: The Wikimedia Foundation is staking out a middle ground in a group of landmark AI copyright cases, pushing courts to legally protect large language models (LLMs) training on copyrighted work - but not…
articles.body: The Wikimedia Foundation is staking out a middle ground in a group of landmark AI copyright cases, pushing courts to legally protect large language models (LLMs) training on copyrighted work - but not chatbots regurgitating that work to users. An overly black-and-white ruling, it says, could either deprive Wikipedians of useful AI-based tools or endanger the open web. In an amicus brief filed Friday, the nonprofit behind Wikipedia weighed in on a set of lawsuits pitting publishers including The New York Times against OpenAI and Microsoft, taking neither side. articles.body: APOD Science APOD APOD: 2026 October 30 –… Today’s APOD Archive Submissions Index Search Calendar RSS Education About Discuss APOD Astronomy Picture of the Day Discover the cosmos! Each day a different image or photograph of our fascinating universe is featured, along with a brief explanation written by a professional astronomer. Haunting the Cepheus Flare Explanation: Spooky shapes seem to haunt this dusty expanse, drifting through the night in the royal constellation Cepheus . Of course, the shapes are cosmic dust clouds visible in dimly reflected starlight. Far from your own neighborhood , they lurk above the plane of the Milky Way at the edge of the Cepheus Flare molecular cloud complex some 1,200 light-years away.
